subject: math
cluster: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations
intro: Two numbers describe a data set: a measure of center tells you a typical value, and a measure of variability tells you how spread out the values are. Center includes the mean $\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum x_i}{n}$ and the median (the middle of the ordered list). Variability includes the range ($\max - \min$), the interquartile range $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$, and the mean absolute deviation $\text{MAD} = \dfrac{\sum |x_i - \bar{x}|}{n}$. To compare two random samples, look at both a center and a spread. A powerful comparison is the difference in means measured in MADs, $\dfrac{|\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2|}{\text{MAD}}$, which tells you how separated the two groups really are.

items.prompt: Find the mean of the data set $\{6, 9, 9, 12, 14\}$.

steps: Add the values: $6 + 9 + 9 + 12 + 14 = 50$.
Count the values: there are $n = 5$ values.
Divide the sum by the count: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{50}{5}$.
Compute: $\bar{x} = 10$.

items.prompt: Find the median and the range of the data set $\{14, 3, 9, 7, 11, 5, 8\}$.

steps: Order the data from least to greatest: $3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 14$.
There are $n = 7$ values (odd), so the median is the middle one, the $4$th value.
The median is $8$.
The range is $\max - \min = 14 - 3 = 11$.

items.prompt: Find the interquartile range (IQR) of the data set $\{2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14\}$.

steps: The data is already ordered: $2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14$.
The median is the middle value $8$. It splits the data into a lower half $\{2, 5, 6\}$ and an upper half $\{9, 12, 14\}$.
$Q_1$ is the median of the lower half: $Q_1 = 5$.
$Q_3$ is the median of the upper half: $Q_3 = 12$.
Compute the IQR: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 12 - 5 = 7$.

items.prompt: Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the data set $\{3, 5, 8, 8\}$.

steps: Find the mean: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{3 + 5 + 8 + 8}{4} = \dfrac{24}{4} = 6$.
Find each absolute deviation from the mean: $|3 - 6| = 3$, $|5 - 6| = 1$, $|8 - 6| = 2$, $|8 - 6| = 2$.
Add the absolute deviations: $3 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 8$.
Divide by the count $n = 4$: $\text{MAD} = \dfrac{8}{4} = 2$.

items.prompt: A random sample of plants grown with Fertilizer A has mean height $\bar{x}_A = 22$ cm with $\text{MAD} = 3$ cm. A random sample grown with Fertilizer B has mean height $\bar{x}_B = 16$ cm with $\text{MAD} = 3$ cm. Which fertilizer typically produces taller plants, and how many MADs apart are the two means?

steps: Compare the centers: $\bar{x}_A = 22$ cm is greater than $\bar{x}_B = 16$ cm, so Fertilizer A typically produces taller plants.
Both samples have the same $\text{MAD} = 3$ cm, so the two groups are equally consistent.
Find the difference in means: $|\bar{x}_A - \bar{x}_B| = |22 - 16| = 6$ cm.
Express that difference as a multiple of the MAD: $\dfrac{6}{3} = 2$.
The means are $2$ MADs apart. Because the random samples come from each population, this separation suggests Fertilizer A really does grow taller plants on average.
solution.answer: Fertilizer A is taller; the means are $2$ MADs apart.

items.prompt: Find the mean of the data set $\{4, 7, 7, 10, 12\}$.
items.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many values there are.

steps: Add the values: $4 + 7 + 7 + 10 + 12 = 40$.
There are $n = 5$ values.
Divide: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8$.

items.prompt: Find the median of the data set $\{15, 4, 9, 2, 10, 6, 13\}$.
items.hint: Order the data first, then find the middle value.

steps: There are $n = 7$ values (odd), so the median is the $4$th value.
The median is $9$.

items.prompt: Find the interquartile range (IQR) of the data set $\{1, 4, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19\}$.
items.hint: Split the ordered data into a lower half and an upper half, then find $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.

steps: The data is ordered and has $n = 8$ values (even). Split into a lower half $\{1, 4, 4, 7\}$ and an upper half $\{10, 13, 16, 19\}$.
$Q_1$ is the median of the lower half: $Q_1 = \dfrac{4 + 4}{2} = 4$.
$Q_3$ is the median of the upper half: $Q_3 = \dfrac{13 + 16}{2} = 14.5$.
Compute the IQR: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 14.5 - 4 = 10.5$.

items.prompt: Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the data set $\{2, 4, 9, 9\}$.
items.hint: First find the mean, then average the absolute distances from the mean.

steps: Find the mean: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{2 + 4 + 9 + 9}{4} = \dfrac{24}{4} = 6$.
Divide by $n = 4$: $\text{MAD} = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3$.

items.prompt: A random sample of words from a children's book has mean length $\bar{x}_1 = 4$ letters with $\text{MAD} = 1$ letter. A random sample from a science magazine has mean length $\bar{x}_2 = 7$ letters with $\text{MAD} = 1$ letter. Which source typically uses longer words, and how many MADs apart are the means?
items.hint: Compare the means to decide which is longer, then compute $\dfrac{|\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2|}{\text{MAD}}$.

steps: Compare the centers: $\bar{x}_2 = 7 > \bar{x}_1 = 4$, so the science magazine typically uses longer words.
Find the difference in means: $|\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2| = |4 - 7| = 3$ letters.
Express as a multiple of the MAD: $\dfrac{3}{1} = 3$, so the means are $3$ MADs apart.
Because both samples were chosen at random, this large separation supports the inference that the magazine's words are typically longer than the book's.
solution.answer: The science magazine; the means are $3$ MADs apart.
